content:
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platform
Rijeka, Croatia | lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

PROFILE
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses across payments, e-commerce and logistics. Experienced in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka and AWS, with a strong background in dimensional data modeling, data quality and large-scale batch and streaming pipelines. Focused on reliable, well-tested systems, clear data contracts and reusable platform capabilities. MSc in Computer Science; AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer - Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace), Rijeka | 03/2022 - present
- Own ingestion and orchestration for the company data platform, operating approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake.
- Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to more than 420 dbt models with tests and documentation; introduced incremental models and state:modified CI in GitHub Actions, reducing nightly warehouse builds from 5h10 to 1h35.
- Designed JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately 9 per month to 2 per month.
- Designed and built a Kafka event pipeline using Kafka Connect and Snowpipe Streaming for shipment tracking, handling approximately 30 million events per day with under 2-minute p95 end-to-end latency; added dead-letter and replay tooling.
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts from the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
- Optimized Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and unused-table usage, reducing monthly spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 in 2024.
- Participate in the data platform on-call rotation (one week in six); mentor two mid-level data engineers and run weekly platform office hours.

Data Engineer - Kovalent Pay (payments startup), Zagreb | 09/2019 - 02/2022
- Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files from S3 daily; reduced finance team's manual month-end reconciliation from approximately three days to four hours.
- Designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams.
- Established Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
- Developed an internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access, adopted by four teams.

Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer - Adria Retail Group, Split | 06/2017 - 08/2019
- Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL processes feeding an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
- Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron, making data loads easier to debug and change.
- Built Power BI reports for store operations across more than 40 stores.

SELECTED OPEN-SOURCE & COMMUNITY CONTRIBUTIONS
- Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider for a SaaS CRM API, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests (Python, pytest, 2023).
- Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup (2024).
- Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since 2021.

EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) - Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries

CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024

SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data engineering: Airflow, dbt, PySpark, Spark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Great Expectations
Warehousing & databases: Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server
Cloud & infrastructure: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, senior-level CV with clear progression, excellent quantified achievements, and highly relevant experience in data platforms, payments, orchestration, cloud warehousing, streaming, data quality, and open-source practices. The experience bullets are specific and outcome-oriented: reducing warehouse runtime, lowering cloud spend, reducing incidents, handling 30 million events per day, and reducing reconciliation work from three days to four hours all create strong credibility. The structure is professional and easy to scan, with a concise profile, reverse-chronological experience, relevant community contributions, education, certification, skills, and languages. The CV also demonstrates ownership through platform on-call work, mentoring, office hours, and production operations. There are no apparent unsupported claims or hallucinated skills when cross-referenced against the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, standard text formatting, searchable technology names, clear dates, and no tables, graphics, icons, or complex layout elements that would impair parsing. It includes strong matches for the advertised stack, including Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, Docker, CI/CD-related GitHub Actions, cloud warehousing, data quality, and dimensional data modeling. AI screening probability is high because the document presents a coherent senior data-platform profile with measurable production-scale evidence rather than only a keyword list. A small ATS improvement would be to include the exact phrases "dimensional modeling" and "CI/CD" in the Skills section, since both appear in the job description and are supported by the candidate's experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The alignment is excellent. The CV clearly shows experience designing, building, and operating a production data platform at scale through ownership of approximately 140 Airflow DAGs, Snowflake ingestion, Kafka streaming, CDC, data contracts, CI checks, and on-call operations. Python and SQL are supported by multiple years of production work, Python libraries and scripts, PySpark, dbt, stored-procedure migration, and large-scale warehouse and reconciliation workloads. Strong dimensional modeling is shown through the Redshift star schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables. AWS, Snowflake, EMR, S3, Glue, Lambda, Docker, and Terraform provide credible comparable-cloud experience despite the absence of Google Cloud. Curiosity about architecture and open-source practices is particularly well demonstrated through the data-contracts meetup talk and two merged Airflow-provider pull requests. Professional English is supported by the stated C1 level and international technical experience. The CV also supports the company's Ownership, Together, and Pace signals through on-call responsibility, mentoring, platform office hours, cross-team data contracts, incident reduction, and simplifying or accelerating data workflows. Graph modeling and Portuguese are not evidenced in the candidate material; these are genuine requirement gaps rather than CV defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Skills section, change the current "Data engineering:" line to include the supported phrase "dimensional modeling"; for example: "Data engineering & modeling: Airflow, dbt, PySpark, Spark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Great Expectations, dimensional modeling." This makes the advertised requirement directly searchable while remaining truthful.
2. In the Skills section under "Cloud & infrastructure," change "GitHub Actions" to "CI/CD: GitHub Actions" or revise the line to read "Cloud, infrastructure & CI/CD: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions." The candidate's state:modified CI workflow and CI checks support this terminology.
3. In the Experience section under Lukovac Freight Hub, consider changing "Optimized Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and unused-table usage" to "Optimized Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend settings and unused-table usage" for slightly clearer wording. Keep the existing $38,000-to-$24,000 monthly cost result, which is a strong achievement.
